html:
A war of about fifteen years between Athens and its allies on one side and Sparta, Corinth and their allies on the other, from about 460 to 445 BCE.

After the Spartan earthquake and the insult to Cimon, Athens allied with Argos and with Megara, Corinth's neighbour. Fighting came in bursts:

  • Athens built the Long Walls linking the city to its port
  • Sparta won at Tanagra in 457 BCE, but Athens took control of Boeotia soon after
  • a large Athenian force sent to help a revolt in Egypt against Persia was destroyed around 454 BCE
  • Athens lost Boeotia again at Coronea in 447 BCE

Neither side could beat the other. The Thirty Years' Peace of 446 to 445 BCE split Greece into an Athenian sea empire and a Spartan land alliance. Pericles rose to lead Athens in these years. The peace held only fourteen years before the great Peloponnesian War began in 431 BCE.
sum: A war of about fifteen years between Athens and its allies on one side and Sparta, Corinth and their allies on the other, from about 460 to 445 BCE.
